name: wire-v1
_comment: The /api/zones shape the published 1.x clients can consume. Shared by 1.0.4
and 1.1.0 — their decode surface is byte-identical (verified 2026-08-08: the
diffs between those tags are `.use {}` resource-closing in ZoneApi.kt, an
avgSpeed change on a non-wire type, and doc comments).
Every rule below is transcribed from the source files in `derived_from` and
is proved by a fixture under `fixtures/` — see contracts/README.md. A rule no
fixture can demonstrate is a guess; do not add one without its fixture.
Note `zone_schema` serializes with exclude_none=True, so a null field is
OMITTED from the wire entirely. `required` therefore means 'must not be None'.

derived_from._comment: decode_surface files are fingerprinted by check_drift.py; render_rules are recorded for provenance only — they contain no field declarations, and their constraint (MapLibre's LineString arity) is proved on-device by qa/scenarios/sync/zones_all_usable.py instead.

constraints.why: MapLibre rejects the ENTIRE zone FeatureCollection on one invalid LineString ('must have two or more coordinate points'), so a single degenerate zone blanks the whole map on Android 1.x. Gson parses it happily, so this is a render rule the decoder cannot catch.
Both clients subscript point[0]/point[1] unguarded when building geometry; a short pair traps on iOS and throws on Android.

A (0, 0) endpoint is the placeholder a BG TOLL zone keeps when it fails to merge with a coordinate-bearing source. The engine can never detect such a zone, and it drags map camera fits toward the Gulf of Guinea.
Zero or negative distance divides through the average-speed and remainder math.
A 0 km/h limit reads as permanently over-limit for that vehicle class. Android 1.x Gson zero-fills an absent key, which is how this arises in practice.
